_comment: RELEASE NOTES. This is the only file to edit when a change should be announced to users.
JSON has no comments, so every key that starts with an underscore is a comment: the loader in core/release_notes.py ignores it. Keep your notes in these keys.
HOW IT IS SHOWN: each signed-in person sees the changes for their own audience in a card at the bottom right of their page, until they close it. Closing is saved for that one account.
RULES (checked by tests/current/test_release_notes_contract.py, so a mistake fails the tests):
1. 'releases' is ordered newest first. Each 'version' is dotted numbers (for example 2.20.26.1) and must go UP for each new release.
The app's current version is the newest release's version. Do not edit it anywhere else.
A change only ever shows to its own audience. A student change never appears on a parent's dashboard, and the reverse.
3. 'text' is the whole message, in plain language for the people who read it. Write it so it makes sense on its own.
4. 'help' is ONLY for 'staff' changes. It must be the slug of a page in the staff guide (see GUIDE_PAGES in blueprints/school/guide.py),
for example 'students' or 'results-report-cards'. Parents and students cannot open the staff guide, so 'family' and 'student' changes must NOT have 'help'.
5. To announce something new, add a release at the top of 'releases' with a new version, a date (YYYY-MM-DD), a title and its changes.
Do not change the wording of a release that people may already have seen; add a new release instead.

releases.title: Birthday texts, and your own words in every message

changes.text: The school can text each parent a greeting on their child's birthday. Switch it on under Email & SMS, Birthday texts. Greetings go once, on the day, between 7:00 and 20:00, and each one is in the notice log.

Write every email and text message parents receive in your school's own words: Settings, Message wording. Each starts with the standard words, shows what a parent receives, and can go back to the standard words at any time.

Every text message the school sends is now kept to one text (160 characters), so no message costs more than one. The naira sign and curly quotes are sent as plain characters, which keeps texts in the cheapest form.

Settings has a cleaner, more compact design: it opens on one index of every setting with its state and what needs attention, the list stays beside each setting, and on a phone a single button opens the list. Press / to find a setting.
On your child's birthday, the school may send you a short greeting by text message.

releases.title: Entrance practice with hundreds of questions

changes.text: Entrance practice now draws every attempt at random from a question pool: all your earlier entrance papers for that class and subject, your practice bank if you choose one, and hundreds of new ready-made practice questions for Mathematics, English and General Knowledge, for Year 7 / JSS 1 and Year 10 / SSS 1. Practice works from day one, and a retake rarely repeats. Practice Tests shows each subject's pool and lets you set how many questions an attempt draws.
The public entrance practice page has a new compact design in your school's colours: choose the class, see each subject's questions and time, and confirm before the paper opens.
The staff guide now explains how students sit tests and examinations, practice tests, and how candidates sit the entrance examination and its practice, with pictures and troubleshooting for each.

Children preparing for our entrance examination can practise on the school's entrance practice page, with no sign-in: choose the class, then Mathematics, English or General Knowledge. Every attempt brings a new set of questions, marked at the end.

releases.title: The receipt studio

changes.text: Design your school's own payment receipt in the new receipt studio (Design studios): start from one of four templates, add the amount in figures and words, the balance, a PAID stamp, the payment's details, the authorised signature, a barcode, your colours and images, on A5 or A4. Preview it as a PDF, then press Use this design and every receipt follows it - on screen, printed and emailed to parents. A voided receipt is always marked VOID.

The staff guide has a new Design studios page, with pictures of every studio and a step-by-step guide to its tools, and a Troubleshooting section on the pages for ID cards, report cards, receipts, payroll, staff records, leave and staff attendance.

releases.title: Faster report cards and ID cards

changes.text: Report cards in the school's own design are made faster and are smaller to download, a class's ID cards print faster, and report card pages need far less data on a phone.
Report cards open faster and use much less of your phone's data.
Your report card opens faster and uses much less data.

releases.title: Design studios for ID cards and report cards, and a clearer menu

changes.text: Design your school's own report card in the new report card studio: start from one of four templates or a blank page, and add the results table, summary, attendance, position in class, trait ratings, grading key, teacher's comment, the student's details (date of birth, guardian, attendance and more), signatures, shapes, colours and your own images. Preview it as a PDF, then press Use this design and every report card follows it, for staff, parents and students.

The menu is now in two parts: Teaching (your classes, attendance, academics, marking, report cards) and Management (students and parents, staff, finance, design and printing, store and library). The ID card and report card studios are together under Design studios. Both studios fill the whole screen, with every tool in view, and need a computer: on a phone they ask you to use one.

Design your school's ID cards freely in the new ID card studio: text in many fonts, shapes with colours and gradients, the photograph and logo clipped to circles or other shapes, your own uploaded images, the head's and the staff member's signatures, a QR code and a barcode. Move, resize and turn anything, line items up, use layers, undo, zoom, start from a template, and bring back an earlier version. The Details tab puts any of the person's details on the card: for students the date of birth, age, blood group, genotype, guardian and more; for staff the title, job, staff number, date employed and an emergency contact. What you design is exactly what prints.
Staff attendance settings are now in Settings, under Staff & access.

releases.title: Safer staff records, attendance and payroll, and faster pages

changes.text: Nobody in HR changes their own staff record, leave allowance or career, and nobody marks their own attendance by hand: someone else does. The payroll page now shows each person's net pay against the last paid month, so the approver can see a rise at a glance.
Staff leave, payroll and staff records pages load faster, however many staff the school has.

releases.title: Payroll

changes.text: Payroll, under Finance: set each member of staff's salary, allowances, deductions and bank details, then prepare each month's payroll with PAYE, pension and NHF worked out. Someone other than whoever prepared it approves it; then download the bank schedule and the PAYE, pension and NHF returns. Bank details are kept encrypted, and salaries are seen only by those allowed to run payroll. Have the school's accountant check the tax settings first.
My payslips: everyone on the payroll sees and prints their own payslip once the month is approved.

releases.title: Staff clock in on their phones

changes.text: Staff attendance: staff clock in and out on their phones by scanning a code on a screen at the school, which changes every 30 seconds, while their phone confirms they are at the school. Each person clocks in from one phone. The register shows who is in, late, absent or on leave each day, with a month view to download; mark someone in by hand, and decide the corrections staff ask for.

releases.title: Staff records and leave

changes.text: Staff records, under People: a file on everyone the school employs, including staff who never sign in (drivers, cleaners, security). Keep their job, next of kin, qualifications and documents, and their career: promotions, queries, commendations. Career entries are never deleted, only struck out with a reason. The new HR Officer role keeps these records; opening one, or a document, is in the activity log.

Leave: everyone with a staff record now has My leave, to see how many days they have left and ask for leave. Staff leave shows the requests to decide, with each person's balance, and who is on leave now. Set the kinds of leave and their days, and a person's own allowance (days carried over).

releases.title: ID cards, designed by the school

changes.text: Print student and staff ID cards from ID cards in the menu: tick the people, and an A4 sheet of cards opens, with the backs for double-sided printing. Design the cards yourself in the school's colours (photo, name, class, admission number, logo, QR code, signature and more), then lock the design so it cannot change by accident. Each card's QR code opens a page that shows whether it is valid; a lost card can be replaced.

releases.title: Exam mode, and a new page for taking tests

changes.text: Tests and examinations now open in exam mode: full screen, with copying, pasting and right-click turned off, and leaving the page, leaving full screen or opening the paper on another device recorded. Each student gets the questions and options in their own order. See what was recorded on the paper's Exam mode record tab, and choose in its Settings whether to end a paper after a student leaves it a number of times. Exam mode and shuffling can be switched off for any paper.

Tests, examinations and practice tests have a new, simpler page: your card and the question numbers on the left, one question at a time, your answers saved as you go, Mark for review, and a summary before you submit. Tests and examinations open in full screen in exam mode: stay on the page until you submit, because leaving it is recorded for your teacher.

releases.title: Tests and examinations sat on paper

changes.text: A test or examination can now be sat on paper instead of on the computer. Print the question paper, and an answer booklet for each student with their name, admission number and photograph already filled in, then enter the marks for the whole class on one sheet under To mark. Absent students are recorded as absent. A paper sat on paper is never shown to students online.

releases.title: Theory questions, marked by the subject teacher

changes.text: Tests and examinations can now have theory questions as well as objective ones. Students write their answers, which are saved as they type. The subject teacher marks them under To mark in the menu, with an optional marking guide beside each answer, and can move marks between the objective and theory parts of a paper. A result waits, shown as Awaiting marking, until every written answer is marked.

Some tests and examinations now have written (theory) questions. Type your answer in the box: it is saved as you type, so a power cut or a lost connection keeps it. Your teacher marks these answers, so your score appears once they have.
Moving to the next question without choosing an answer now works, instead of showing an error.

releases.title: Billing a class, live and faster

changes.text: Billing a whole class is much faster, and the progress window now lists every student live: who is waiting, who is being billed now, who is billed (with the amount), who was already charged and who could not be billed, with the reason. Press a count at the top to show only those students. Parents' emails and texts now go out in the background, so they no longer slow the billing down.

Questions such as Take these students off the list? and messages such as Please select at least one fee item now appear in the school's own window, in its colours, instead of the browser's grey box. Anything that removes or undoes something is shown in red, and starts on No, go back, so pressing Enter by mistake does nothing.
Questions and messages in the portal now appear in your school's own window, in its colours, instead of the browser's grey box.
Questions in the portal, such as when you submit a test question without choosing an answer, now appear in your school's own window, in its colours.

New students to bill can now bill a class's new students together. Each class with new students not billed yet has a button, such as Bill all 12 together, or tick the students of one class and press Bill ticked students together. Fee structure opens with that class chosen and only those new students on it: pick the fees once and watch each student being billed.

releases.title: Safer sign-ins, Excel imports, and children who have left

changes.text: Bulk imports (students, enrolment history and past results) now take an Excel workbook (.xlsx) as well as a CSV. Only the first sheet is read and formulas are never run; a workbook with macros, or one protected by a password, is refused.
Children who have left the school now have their own section on your Overview, Children who have left the school. Open it to see their fees, receipts, results and report cards, which are all kept.

Sign-ins now end after two hours without using the portal, and after twelve hours in all, so a computer left signed in does not stay open. Signing out now ends that sign-in everywhere. Students and candidates sitting a test or exam are never signed out by this while their paper is running, even after a power cut or a lost connection.

A new password can no longer be one of the commonly guessed ones (such as password123 or school123), a run like 12345678, or contain your username. Repeated wrong passwords from one place, or for one account, now pause sign-in for a few minutes.
A student's fee account now opens only for staff who can see the whole school's finance, the same as the Student accounts page.
For your safety, you are now signed out after two hours without using the portal. A new password can no longer be a commonly guessed one such as password123, or contain your username.

For your safety, you are now signed out after two hours without using the portal, but never while you are writing a test or exam. A new password can no longer be a commonly guessed one such as password123, or contain your login ID.

releases.title: New students to bill

changes.text: New in Finance: New students to bill. Every student admitted from the entrance exam, registered or imported now appears on this list until they have been billed and the bill is paid, so no new student is forgotten. Bill opens Fee structure with the student already chosen, and a student leaves the list on their own once their bill is paid in full. The menu and the Overview show how many are not billed yet.

releases.title: Workspace Home answers one press

changes.text: On Workspace Home, pressing Enter on a workspace now shows a spinner in place of the button's words, and neither button can be pressed again until the page is reloaded, so a workspace can no longer be opened twice by pressing again while it loads.

releases.title: Recording a store payment works again, and workspaces open sooner

changes.text: Choosing a workspace on Workspace Home now opens it in one step instead of two, so it arrives sooner. While it loads, the page already shows the workspace's own menu and the outline of its page, instead of the chooser.

Fixed: in the Store, Record a payment (for an item paid for in cash, by transfer or POS) kept loading after the button was pressed and nothing was saved. It now records the payment, takes the item out of stock and opens the receipt.

releases.title: Class subdivisions and class transfers

changes.text: JSS and SSS classes can now be split into subdivisions, such as JSS 1A and JSS 1B, JSS 2 Gold, or SS 1A (Science). The School Admin sets them up under Settings, Class subdivisions (with examples on the page) and then locks them. Each subdivision can have its own class teacher, who sees only its students for the register, report card comments and releasing results. Subjects, timetables, fees and results stay whole-class.

Students are placed in subdivisions automatically, in turn, into the one with the fewest students: when a class is split, when a student is added, and when a candidate is admitted from the entrance examination. In SSS, a subdivision with a department only takes students of that department.

New menu item, Class transfers: a JSS or SSS class teacher can ask to move a student to another subdivision, or in SSS to another department. Nothing changes until the class teacher the student would join approves it; the School Admin and head teachers can approve, decline or cancel any transfer.

releases.title: The entrance examination workspace redesigned, SSS departments, and smoother page loading

changes.text: Every page of the Entrance examination workspace now has the same compact look as the School portal: a title line with its buttons, a strip of figures, and dense tables. Candidates and question banks pick their entry level from a row of chips, a question bank lists its questions the way a test does in Academics, and the pages load in place.

Results now has four tabs: By subject, Summary, Rankings and Examination activity, each filtered by entry level and searchable. By subject shows the real figures for every candidate in Mathematics, English and General Knowledge side by side, and its Export CSV and Export JSON buttons now download the results.

Departments for SSS candidates. A candidate entering SSS 1 now chooses a department when registered (Science, Art or Commercial), and their papers include questions from all three departments. On the admissions waitlist each SSS candidate shows their choice beside the department their results fit best, with how they did in each and why. The Department on the admit form starts at that suggestion, and you can change it before admitting. Questions can be tagged with a department on the question form, and the standard SSS 1 General Knowledge bank now comes with Science, Art and Commercial questions.

Moving between pages now shows the outline of a page, softly pulsing under the spinner, from the moment you press until the next page has loaded and been drawn in full; only then does it appear. There is no blank or half-drawn screen in between, also in the installed app.

Fixed: opening the entrance workspace's Overview could quietly drop you out of the workspace, so the next page you opened sent you back to Workspace Home. The school's setup checklist is now shown in the School workspace only.

Moving between pages now shows the outline of a page, softly pulsing under the spinner, until the next page has loaded and been drawn in full, so you never see a blank or half-drawn screen, also in the installed app.

Moving between pages now shows the outline of a page, softly pulsing under the spinner, until the next page has loaded and been drawn in full, so you never see a blank or half-drawn screen, also in the installed app.

releases.title: A steadier spinner, a new workspace page and a tidier sign-in on phones

changes.text: The spinner now stays on screen until the next page is ready. Before, it could disappear while the next page was still on its way, leaving a blank or frozen screen for a second or two, especially in the installed app. Pages also appear sooner, because the browser reuses the files it already has from one page to the next.

The page where you choose a workspace has been redesigned to match the rest of the portal: the school's header bar, then School Portal and Entrance Examination side by side, each with its figures (the session and students enrolled, or candidates registered) and its own Enter button. While the workspace opens, the page dims and its Enter button spins.

Signing in now shows a spinner on the Sign In button while your account is checked. On a phone, the school's logo and name are centred at the top of the sign-in page, and the version and the privacy link sit at the bottom.

Signing in now shows a spinner on the Sign In button while your account is checked, and on a phone the school's logo and name are centred at the top of the sign-in page, with the version and the privacy link at the bottom. Moving between pages keeps the spinner on screen until the next page is ready, so you are never left looking at a blank screen.

Signing in now shows a spinner on the Sign In button while your account is checked, and on a phone the school's logo and name are centred at the top of the sign-in page, with the version and the privacy link at the bottom. Moving between pages keeps the spinner on screen until the next page is ready, so you are never left looking at a blank screen.

releases.title: Clearer portal pages for parents and students

changes.text: The parent portal's pages are simpler and easier to scan. Your children are listed in one table with what each owes, their average and completion, with Profile, Message and Pay fees beside each name. A child's fees, results, work and messages are clear tables, and on a phone each row folds into a short list you can read without scrolling sideways. While a page loads, the page you are on dims under a small spinner and the button you pressed spins, instead of a bar across the top of the screen.

Your student portal pages are simpler and easier to scan. Your assignments, projects and results are clear tables with the due date, status and score side by side, and your tests and examinations are listed with their questions and minutes and an Open button. Your exam timetable and attendance are at the top of your dashboard. While a page loads, the page you are on dims under a small spinner and the button you pressed spins.

The student and parent portal pages now use the same page design as Academics and Finance: a title line with its buttons, the figures strip, panels with compact tables and the same status tags. The coloured banners and tiles are gone. While a portal page loads, it dims under the same spinner the staff pages use.

Moving from one page to another now always shows that it is working: the page you are on dims under a spinner and the button or link you pressed spins until the next page is ready. Before, only some sections did this, and the installed app sat still with no sign of progress when you used the side menu to go to another section, sent a form or opened a workspace. Downloads such as PDFs and CSV files are not affected.
